**Date:** 2026-10-22 · **Tag:** `v6.0.0` · **Baseline:** `v5.2.1` · Major release

npm: `@aztec-foundation/bb.js@6.0.0` (note the new `@aztec-foundation` scope) · crates.io: `barretenberg-rs 6.0.0` · Noir: `v1.0.0-rc.3`

## Summary

v6.0.0 is the protocol, proving system and L1 contracts behind the v6 rollup proposed in [AZUP-3](https://forum.aztec.network/t/azup-3-is-ready-for-proposal/8670). It is a major protocol upgrade: new circuits, a new verification key tree and a new rollup deployment from genesis.

The headline change is the **Fast Inbox** (AZIP-22). L1-to-L2 messages now stream into L2 blocks as nodes see them on L1, instead of waiting for an Inbox tree to seal and a two-checkpoint lag, cutting message latency from 24–108 seconds to about 12–30 seconds. It reaches every layer: a rolling-hash Inbox on L1, per-block message bundles and a single variable-size parity proof in the circuits.

Alongside it: a **transaction effects tree** in every block header, a **new protocol nullifier**, a **v3 contract address domain separator**, a large round of **proving system hardening** (much of it developed privately and published with this release), Barretenberg performance work, **Noir 1.0.0 release candidates**, and L1 changes for fees, rewards, provers and staking providers.

This release is aimed at people working on the protocol, the proving system and the L1 contracts. Node operators and application developers should read the [aztec-node v6.0.0 release notes](https://github.com/aztec-labs-eng/aztec-node/releases/tag/v6.0.0) instead.

## What's in AZUP-3

v6 implements the following AZIPs. AZIP-33 and AZIP-34 are carried out by the upgrade payload rather than by contract code.

| [23](https://github.com/AztecProtocol/governance/blob/main/AZIPs/azip-23.md) Protocol Fee Margin | Governance-set margin on the mana base fee, paid to a governance-set recipient. Launches at zero | Rollup ([`f56ff4a`](https://github.com/AztecProtocol/aztec-packages/commit/f56ff4a07831f66a9ad9305c63cd51fd49111da1)) |
| [24](https://github.com/AztecProtocol/governance/blob/main/AZIPs/azip-24.md) First Prover Attribution | The rollup records which prover first proved each checkpoint | Rollup ([#25389](https://github.com/AztecProtocol/aztec-packages/pull/25389)) |
| [25](https://github.com/AztecProtocol/governance/blob/main/AZIPs/azip-25.md) Full Epoch Activity Score | A prover's activity score only increases on a full-epoch proof | Rollup ([`d0c3996`](https://github.com/AztecProtocol/aztec-packages/commit/d0c39965f0edd959e8da9fbdcffb57fbcafe2701)) |

| [27](https://github.com/AztecProtocol/governance/blob/main/AZIPs/azip-27.md) Rate-limited Provider Exits | Attesters can exit their own positions, up to about 5% of the set per governance withdrawal delay | Rollup staking ([#25492](https://github.com/AztecProtocol/aztec-packages/pull/25492)) |

## Breaking changes

- **The foundation npm packages moved to the `@aztec-foundation` scope** ([#25328](https://github.com/AztecProtocol/aztec-packages/pull/25328)): `bb.js`, `bb`, `bb-avm`, `bb-avm-sim`, `cdb`, `wsdb`, `ipc-runtime`, the `noir-*` packages, `l1-artifacts`, `constants-codegen` and the protocol artifacts packages. The `@aztec` scope keeps what was already published.

  ```diff
  -import { Barretenberg } from '@aztec/bb.js';
  +import { Barretenberg } from '@aztec-foundation/bb.js';
  ```

- **Every verification key changes.** New circuits, new flavors and new transcript rules (below) mean v5 proofs and VKs do not verify under v6, and the VK tree root is new.
- **Fiat-Shamir challenges are full-width by default** ([`a69ffdf`](https://github.com/AztecProtocol/aztec-packages/commit/a69ffdf8a1fcfdd5d8bbe0f36e802c3b3df97748)). Challenges are no longer truncated, so transcripts, proofs and VKs from earlier versions are incompatible.
- **Every contract address changes.** The contract address domain separator is bumped to V3 ([#25521](https://github.com/AztecProtocol/aztec-packages/pull/25521)), so the same class, salt, initialization and keys derive a different address than in v5. An address can never be live on two rollups. Protocol contracts keep their magic addresses.
- **Block headers gain a transaction effects tree root** ([`ae2aace`](https://github.com/AztecProtocol/aztec-packages/commit/ae2aaced77714b91130fe053b38e483a33dfe8a7)). Header serialization grows by one field, so every transaction hash, VK, artifact and canonical address changes with it.
- **The protocol nullifier is derived from the tx request's salt alone** ([#25515](https://github.com/AztecProtocol/aztec-packages/pull/25515)). Two requests with the same origin and salt are mutually exclusive, and the siloed `protocol_nullifier` replaces `tx_request_salt` in the private call inputs.
- **`MAX_APPS_PER_KERNEL` rises from 3 to 5** ([`910504d`](https://github.com/AztecProtocol/aztec-packages/commit/910504d638d047b42f33dcc5774bbce4681b6c22)), and kernels use custom arithmetic gates ([`b7433c0`](https://github.com/AztecProtocol/aztec-packages/commit/b7433c03ec95e94f9a62e35b312647a43ea14989)).
- **The AVM's Poseidon2 permutation is re-optimised** ([`ce692ca`](https://github.com/AztecProtocol/aztec-packages/commit/ce692ca06170d28189cbea3bc15107aa639aeb48)), and the AVM now has at most 4 registers ([`9b3753f`](https://github.com/AztecProtocol/aztec-packages/commit/9b3753f99cf983140f463df86da82530ba49cb96)).

## Proving system (Barretenberg)

**Chonk (client IVC)**

- **Per-kind circuit flavors.** Apps and kernels now have their own flavors, `MegaApp` and `MegaKernel` ([`ff378cb`](https://github.com/AztecProtocol/aztec-packages/commit/ff378cbed5b00a9071c34f09b3a88a37b1162a31)), with a `CircuitKind` carried from the PXE through bb.js and bbapi. Protocol VKs are computed per kind at the source, replacing `--use_zk_flavor`.
- **One multilinear-batching sumcheck per kernel** ([`635a9cf`](https://github.com/AztecProtocol/aztec-packages/commit/635a9cf2cbf53d6aea15f0e90e0e4aaf32497676)).
- **Custom arithmetic gates for kernels** ([`b7433c0`](https://github.com/AztecProtocol/aztec-packages/commit/b7433c03ec95e94f9a62e35b312647a43ea14989)), and room for 5 apps per kernel instead of 3 ([`910504d`](https://github.com/AztecProtocol/aztec-packages/commit/910504d638d047b42f33dcc5774bbce4681b6c22)).
- **ROM tables via logup** ([`d3e42f9`](https://github.com/AztecProtocol/aztec-packages/commit/d3e42f9d3a31ee0ccd8a36055a13f69508d3a65f)).
- **Cheaper Poseidon2:** two fewer rows per permutation ([`f14df1d`](https://github.com/AztecProtocol/aztec-packages/commit/f14df1d3b85a3c841f0188dfbef88d85601f087a)) and batched sponge absorbs ([`f7b101b`](https://github.com/AztecProtocol/aztec-packages/commit/f7b101b54c724efe3a49309c656a085e6c5c07aa)).

**PCS, IPA and the Grumpkin side**

- **TripleIPA for the ECCVM** ([`bcb979d`](https://github.com/AztecProtocol/aztec-packages/commit/bcb979da4dc8c9be40b50cc1a538e8506c81536d)), with fused IPA folds and a short-scalar IPA SRS fold.
- **A sparse ZK masking polynomial in Shplemini** ([`1a42ab0`](https://github.com/AztecProtocol/aztec-packages/commit/1a42ab0261019fbb872abf39da92792b00a55c8c)), and Libra masking with `L = 4` on Grumpkin ([`19052d3`](https://github.com/AztecProtocol/aztec-packages/commit/19052d3f7f08e1401a93cc1ad8f0987db746fe43)).
- **ECCVM and Translator sumcheck optimizations** ([#23615](https://github.com/AztecProtocol/aztec-packages/pull/23615)), plus general sumcheck round and relation evaluation speed-ups.
- **The Grumpkin SRS is anchored to pinned chunk hashes on load** ([#23587](https://github.com/AztecProtocol/aztec-packages/pull/23587)).

**Performance**

- **A rewritten Pippenger MSM** ([`3c7386e`](https://github.com/AztecProtocol/aztec-packages/commit/3c7386eb7bbddec89bb6548982583eb65bb563bc)) and Booth-sliced element MSMs ([#23691](https://github.com/AztecProtocol/aztec-packages/pull/23691)).
- **WASM SIMD throughout the prover:** a 5-wide `VectorField` primitive, Montgomery multiplication, row-parallel sumcheck univariates, and SIMD Gemini folds and `partially_evaluate`.
- **Faster circuit construction** ([`398a5e6`](https://github.com/AztecProtocol/aztec-packages/commit/398a5e627742b7fe37d913699503a0550dffd65c)): arithmetic, tiled gate storage and containers.

**AVM**

- **A specialized MegaAVM flavor** ([`a32b5b8`](https://github.com/AztecProtocol/aztec-packages/commit/a32b5b84f8e2276a836e9685de313de31c01d8c8)), per-column public-input sizes in the recursive verifier, and granular destination selectors for precomputed subtraces.
- **The TypeScript AVM simulator is gone.** Simulation runs in the native `bb-avm-sim` service over generated IPC bindings ([`96082e3`](https://github.com/AztecProtocol/aztec-packages/commit/96082e32ec5216cb0dc32fda6f3f9098b8184e30)), alongside a `wsdb` world-state service and the new `ipc-runtime`.
- **Fixes from the Honk audit** ([`2c6023a`](https://github.com/AztecProtocol/aztec-packages/commit/2c6023ab998e3077c21e2fd1dd3077b81664bd80)).

## Soundness and security hardening

A large set of proving system and circuit fixes was developed in a private branch while the v6 circuits were being finalized. It is public with this release, and the mainnet v6 verifier and VK tree are built from it. Each item below links the commit.

**Verifier and transcript strictness**

- **Recursive pairing accumulators with a mixed point at infinity are rejected** ([`3763de6`](https://github.com/AztecProtocol/aztec-packages/commit/3763de6f0fb1102a92acd42aaa66a3cee67acd40)). This is the v6 counterpart of [GHSA-2hc8-mq24-76v2](https://github.com/AztecProtocol/aztec-packages/security/advisories/GHSA-2hc8-mq24-76v2) (high) and [GHSA-73xc-j27q-wg75](https://github.com/AztecProtocol/aztec-packages/security/advisories/GHSA-73xc-j27q-wg75) (medium), both fixed for v5 in v5.2.1.
- **PCS pairing points at infinity fail verification** ([`5b16bcd`](https://github.com/AztecProtocol/aztec-packages/commit/5b16bcdb1d87357514a89cc39ca694232c722352)) rather than being accepted or aborting.
- **Verifiers consume each proof segment exactly** ([`cd61020`](https://github.com/AztecProtocol/aztec-packages/commit/cd610200949048ca8915b886ee8e82657cef2c2c)), and native verifiers **reject trailing data** after a proof ([`94581fe`](https://github.com/AztecProtocol/aztec-packages/commit/94581fe61bf257243319efc061dbe3ea69976045)).
- **Pairing points are aggregated with short scalar multiplications** on Ultra ([`2b0c0b4`](https://github.com/AztecProtocol/aztec-packages/commit/2b0c0b42bc112922a0e6f26aebb7d5a43e9a442e)).
- **IPA challenge handling is tightened** ([`1b33386`](https://github.com/AztecProtocol/aztec-packages/commit/1b33386f89d2d50dc8c6ed1ca2eccad0d96f6e5b)), and verifier and prover validation strengthened across flavors ([`74cbbff`](https://github.com/AztecProtocol/aztec-packages/commit/74cbbff6d954fa72231275c38c5e39d833e4964d)).
- **Flavor selectors must be compatible with their relations** ([`6bbfc20`](https://github.com/AztecProtocol/aztec-packages/commit/6bbfc2052a596dd29d8166ec8f401a573f31918b)).

**Constraint fixes**

- **ECCVM:** scalar limbs and first-row translation values are now constrained ([`3472adc`](https://github.com/AztecProtocol/aztec-packages/commit/3472adc4ac319ce1e97668f07c575f71cd3839c7)); queue reconstruction and IPA inputs are validated ([`8c9f71b`](https://github.com/AztecProtocol/aztec-packages/commit/8c9f71bfb910a1520d024f458a9c4fae20c848cd)); MSM constraints are updated ([`224b033`](https://github.com/AztecProtocol/aztec-packages/commit/224b03373ec2d8a43cc228adb600aaf34c50137c)).
- **Translator:** boundary constraints updated ([`d3020cb`](https://github.com/AztecProtocol/aztec-packages/commit/d3020cb2611d248cea0d2ef9583cc145dc45fefd)).
- **Databus:** constraints strengthened ([`08f20ae`](https://github.com/AztecProtocol/aztec-packages/commit/08f20ae7966e08f06b23e5cd01fdf891b91b60b7)).
- **Batch merge:** accumulator boundaries validated ([`d2469f2`](https://github.com/AztecProtocol/aztec-packages/commit/d2469f280c543ee25575cab9aa6d2c2fe23b3dea)).
- **Chonk:** proof boundaries ([`6d7fd08`](https://github.com/AztecProtocol/aztec-packages/commit/6d7fd083bec34c7c3deb4f5ffbb404782db6d055)) and the proving and mock-verification paths hardened ([`80e6dca`](https://github.com/AztecProtocol/aztec-packages/commit/80e6dcae04e5e91f3a806b556db93e93c63ad09e)).
- **Constant-point MSMs:** validation strengthened ([`dfa66b7`](https://github.com/AztecProtocol/aztec-packages/commit/dfa66b7b4ce98714380e7875fed8203060df8234)).

**Input validation**

- **Serialization, SRS and crypto inputs** are validated before use ([`e8a1119`](https://github.com/AztecProtocol/aztec-packages/commit/e8a1119d1bc11ec2a62c10b1a0deb63156429b0d)), and msgpack errors and SRS size are checked before allocation ([#25487](https://github.com/AztecProtocol/aztec-packages/pull/25487)).
- **`FieldSponge`** is bound to the permutation's state width ([`ca59e1c`](https://github.com/AztecProtocol/aztec-packages/commit/ca59e1c53d7c124558e40144b5e9bfccbc5c7806)).

**Protocol circuits**

- **Kernels:** stricter tail array validation ([`bec1093`](https://github.com/AztecProtocol/aztec-packages/commit/bec10934b1abc910f9ac5cfa763c63533b501461)); claimed lengths asserted against array capacity in the tail's dense, trimmed and sorted helpers ([`87b10ed`](https://github.com/AztecProtocol/aztec-packages/commit/87b10ed2eb6c8d99f2d40abc4d5d9ae91da5887e)); `claimed_revertible_counter` bounded in the init circuit ([`26f3e5c`](https://github.com/AztecProtocol/aztec-packages/commit/26f3e5c6e981b3766f78d9bca589693431187359)); scoped metadata preserved through reset ([`6088fa8`](https://github.com/AztecProtocol/aztec-packages/commit/6088fa89a0b4bb049f7ee827c40d44be30d64776)); zero-valued settled read requests rejected ([`9929a81`](https://github.com/AztecProtocol/aztec-packages/commit/9929a8195613b3c520f407bb4ef5a01f03266f08)).
- **A surviving nullifier link may only resolve to a non-revertible note hash** ([#25579](https://github.com/AztecProtocol/aztec-packages/pull/25579)).
- **Rollup:** private log padding validated ([`b8cfcc1`](https://github.com/AztecProtocol/aztec-packages/commit/b8cfcc101652480cf5f38af2d9e028cbfd5d2b74)); blob points must be canonically encoded ([`7e6ff7b`](https://github.com/AztecProtocol/aztec-packages/commit/7e6ff7b04bc182786d6209bf7148a86728242f43)); contract class log lengths must be canonical ([`1815fd5`](https://github.com/AztecProtocol/aztec-packages/commit/1815fd5c09a67e8254af7d8d4c788c01cd807683)).
- **Serialization:** `Option` must be canonically serialized ([`41ecf22`](https://github.com/AztecProtocol/aztec-packages/commit/41ecf22b90ec8731969d7ff057406de4d6e2544d)), and `BoundedVec` lengths are validated in protocol serde ([`cda1c77`](https://github.com/AztecProtocol/aztec-packages/commit/cda1c77cdecd09dc7c88b395a4b155cf92bbe73e)).
- **Bigcurve and bignum fixes**, with their tests now running in CI ([`e078f15`](https://github.com/AztecProtocol/aztec-packages/commit/e078f15728bb585b40e9325ddffc8d2cc66ebb37)).
- **AVM simulator:** hashmap keys hash the full `u128` ([`f5d6874`](https://github.com/AztecProtocol/aztec-packages/commit/f5d687452d3ea1570d5f71c3d1f1a9a5bd789210)).

## Protocol circuits

- **Fast Inbox circuits.** L1-to-L2 messages arrive in per-block bundles ([`a6f0cc5`](https://github.com/AztecProtocol/aztec-packages/commit/a6f0cc55f6707826550b282e56a12e329a536eef)), proven by a single variable-size `InboxParity` proof per checkpoint ([`420d574`](https://github.com/AztecProtocol/aztec-packages/commit/420d57449bfca99c192619abe6cb3b061479d24a)), with variants for sizes 4 and 16. Non-first blocks can consume messages from the same block ([`94c4a8e`](https://github.com/AztecProtocol/aztec-packages/commit/94c4a8e0b2cdb6460c7cddefc895589bd56130ce)), and a new `block_root_msgs_only_rollup` circuit handles blocks with messages but no transactions ([`6847d80`](https://github.com/AztecProtocol/aztec-packages/commit/6847d80c00812aa945751290b0c16342d9646bbe)). Blocks per checkpoint are capped, empty blocks are allowed anywhere, and the block-root variants are merged ([`f341571`](https://github.com/AztecProtocol/aztec-packages/commit/f3415717ab1f81d96fdda8d959d5d2c4c29b865d)).
- **The Inbox rolling-hash chain is domain-separated** ([`a96bcfd`](https://github.com/AztecProtocol/aztec-packages/commit/a96bcfde13ffac54d99c6c1cc598c165ec983618)).
- **Transaction effects tree** ([`ae2aace`](https://github.com/AztecProtocol/aztec-packages/commit/ae2aaced77714b91130fe053b38e483a33dfe8a7)): one leaf per transaction, binding its hash to a structured hash of its effects. A block header alone now proves inclusion and exact effects with a short membership proof.
- **Protocol contracts call the protocol oracles** ([#25526](https://github.com/AztecProtocol/aztec-packages/pull/25526)), and their registration nullifiers are seeded at genesis ([#25497](https://github.com/AztecProtocol/aztec-packages/pull/25497)).
- **The teardown call's AVM startup gas is charged** ([#25536](https://github.com/AztecProtocol/aztec-packages/pull/25536)).
- **Blob fractions are derived by halving the roots of unity** ([`070b810`](https://github.com/AztecProtocol/aztec-packages/commit/070b810c07886de1fc9bf589aa643267fbab55b5)).
- **`poseidon2_hash_bytes` does not commit to the byte length**, now documented ([#25566](https://github.com/AztecProtocol/aztec-packages/pull/25566)). Callers that need length binding must add it themselves.
- **The protocol artifacts are published to npm** ([#25075](https://github.com/AztecProtocol/aztec-packages/pull/25075)), and constants are generated by a standalone `constants-codegen` package.

## Noir

- **Noir moves from `v1.0.0-beta.25` to `v1.0.0-rc.3`**, the first Noir 1.0 release candidates ([#25511](https://github.com/AztecProtocol/aztec-packages/pull/25511)).
- **`noir-lang/poseidon` is now v0.4.0.**
- **Circuits execute with `noir-execute`.** The standalone `acvm` binary is no longer shipped.

## L1 contracts

**Fast Inbox (AZIP-22)**

- **The Inbox keeps rolling-hash buckets** alongside its frontier trees ([`d627406`](https://github.com/AztecProtocol/aztec-packages/commit/d627406d69e8fdbd0ca44885f57f22f91dbb1675)), and consensus moves to the streaming Inbox ([`a703815`](https://github.com/AztecProtocol/aztec-packages/commit/a703815349c3cf21c11c0c08e74d54e0805f28ce)).
- **Buckets are evicted only after their messages are consumed by a proven checkpoint** ([`455099a`](https://github.com/AztecProtocol/aztec-packages/commit/455099a3928facedd6d3ee0b4d0b55bec943c034)).
- **The censorship cutoff is derived from the configured Ethereum slot duration.**
- **`MessageSent` emits the full message**, and `getState` returns the Inbox's full live position.

**Proofs and provers**

- **Epoch proofs verify only new headers** ([#25404](https://github.com/AztecProtocol/aztec-packages/pull/25404)), `submitProof` takes only the new headers ([#25419](https://github.com/AztecProtocol/aztec-packages/pull/25419)), and full-epoch proof overhead is reduced ([#25406](https://github.com/AztecProtocol/aztec-packages/pull/25406), [#25386](https://github.com/AztecProtocol/aztec-packages/pull/25386)).
- **Early proof submission can no longer be used to grief other provers** ([#25582](https://github.com/AztecProtocol/aztec-packages/pull/25582)).
- **First prover attribution** (AZIP-24, [#25389](https://github.com/AztecProtocol/aztec-packages/pull/25389)) and **a full-epoch-only activity score** (AZIP-25).

**Fees and rewards**

- **Protocol fee margin** (AZIP-23): a governance-set margin and recipient on the mana base fee, launching at zero.
- **Pluggable sequencer reward calculator** (AZIP-31, [#25571](https://github.com/AztecProtocol/aztec-packages/pull/25571)). A calculator that reverts or misbehaves falls back to the default reward and never blocks a proof.
- **Glamsterdam gas constants** (AZIP-35, [#25509](https://github.com/AztecProtocol/aztec-packages/pull/25509)), and a 90/10 sequencer/prover reward split (AZIP-30).

**Staking**

- **Rate-limited attester-initiated exits** (AZIP-27, [#25492](https://github.com/AztecProtocol/aztec-packages/pull/25492)). An attester, or a relayer carrying attester-signed EIP-712 authorizations, can start an exit. The stake still goes to the withdrawer.
  - At most `floor((N - 1) / 20)` exits per rolling governance withdrawal delay, never below the target committee size.
  - Only on the canonical, latest rollup.

**Deployment and upgrade**

- **The v6 upgrade deploy script, `V6UpgradePayload` and runbook** ([#25601](https://github.com/AztecProtocol/aztec-packages/pull/25601)). The rollup is owned by governance from construction, the escape hatch is installed by the payload, and the payload refuses to run unless its predecessor is still canonical.
- **The rollup config is held in immutables** ([#25314](https://github.com/AztecProtocol/aztec-packages/pull/25314)), and admin paths moved into libraries to fit the EIP-170 size limit.
- **The generic deployer refuses unusable rollup configuration** ([#25520](https://github.com/AztecProtocol/aztec-packages/pull/25520)), and its docs now state it is the test and testnet deployer, not the mainnet path.

## Packaging

- **All foundation npm packages are published under `@aztec-foundation`** ([#25328](https://github.com/AztecProtocol/aztec-packages/pull/25328)), with npm provenance from GitHub Actions.
- **`bb` and `bb-avm` ship as per-platform npm packages**, byte-identical to the release tarballs, and `bb-avm` now builds for arm64 Linux ([#25120](https://github.com/AztecProtocol/aztec-packages/pull/25120)).
- **The AVM CDB server bindings are published as `@aztec-foundation/cdb`** ([#25098](https://github.com/AztecProtocol/aztec-packages/pull/25098)).
- **`barretenberg-rs` is published to crates.io.**
- **`l1-artifacts` is a standalone npm package**, carrying the full `l1-contracts` Solidity tree and compiled ABIs.

## Protocol constants

The mainnet v6 rollup ([`0xE37A2663Cc9c119BA41572C40fAb0bbb23a5402f`](https://etherscan.io/address/0xE37A2663Cc9c119BA41572C40fAb0bbb23a5402f), rollup version `2070860440`) was deployed from this release's circuits:

```
vk root               0x22fff5de6ce590153df4468f7f0b152188a803d91b3c9c648b91d93d5913f219
protocol contracts    0x0f54271c52865841a77aaa66036eed901aff22fdce9f08e123ec8b205c9854d7
genesis archive root  0x29eb2c527f8d45276430363214e6c8d709ef3f657a3670ebac3179373d41e5c4
verifier VK_HASH      0x1fd4eb1d14be45e05dc78c448eb4f29d7f63e4de95129c4a5e1058cd9837f8a6
```

The epoch proof verifier is pinned at `l1-contracts/script/deploy/HonkVerifier.sol`. Anyone can check its `VK_HASH` against the verified source on Etherscan.

## Reference

- [AZUP-3](https://forum.aztec.network/t/azup-3-is-ready-for-proposal/8670): the upgrade proposal and its AZIPs.
- [V6 upgrade runbook](https://github.com/AztecProtocol/aztec-packages/blob/v6.0.0/l1-contracts/script/deploy/V6_UPGRADE_RUNBOOK.md) and [payload review notes](https://github.com/AztecProtocol/aztec-packages/blob/v6.0.0/l1-contracts/src/periphery/V6UpgradePayload.md).
- [aztec-node v6.0.0](https://github.com/aztec-labs-eng/aztec-node/releases/tag/v6.0.0): the node, Aztec.nr and aztec.js release built on this one.
- [barretenberg v6.0.0](https://github.com/AztecProtocol/barretenberg/releases/tag/v6.0.0): bb binaries.
- [v5.2.1 release notes](https://github.com/AztecProtocol/aztec-packages/releases/tag/v5.2.1): this release's baseline.

# Protocol Changes
* Remove gas rewards: executing a `FunctionCall` no longer pays part of the burned gas back to the contract account as a reward. The `burnt_gas_reward` parameter is changed from 30% (3/10) to 0%. See [HSP-027](https://gov.near.org/t/hsp-027-remove-the-near-developer-gas-rebate/42213)
* Added an `ml_dsa_verify` host function so contracts can verify FIPS 204 ML-DSA-65 signatures on-chain. It takes the signature (3309 bytes), an arbitrary-length message, and the raw 1952-byte public key, each passed either from memory or from a register, and returns 1 for a valid signature or 0 for an invalid one; a wrongly-sized signature or public key aborts the call with `MlDsaVerifyInvalidInput`. The message is verified as-is with an empty context string, so callers must not pre-hash it. It costs a fixed base cost of 540 Ggas and a dynamic per-byte cost of 11 Mgas per byte.
* The per-receipt storage proof limit now applies to every action in a receipt, not just `FunctionCall`. The recorded proof is checked after each action, and a receipt that goes over `per_receipt_storage_proof_size_limit` (4 MB) fails at that action with the new `ReceiptStorageProofSizeExceeded` error; the actions after it do not run. Clients that decode `ActionErrorKind` should expect the new variant. ([#16171](https://github.com/near/nearcore/pull/16171))
* Removed the `DelegateV2` meta-transaction action introduced in 2.13.0. A new transaction or receipt carrying it is now rejected at action validation with the new `ActionsValidationError::RemovedProtocolFeature` error. Its inner nonce advances a gas key of the delegate sender, which the SPICE pending transaction queue does not track, because that queue reads only the outer transaction's signer, public key and nonce index. Gas keys ([NEP-611](https://github.com/near/NEPs/pull/611)) therefore can no longer sign meta transactions at all, since the older `Delegate` action already rejects a gas key signer with `DelegateActionRequiresNonGasKey`. Receipts created before the upgrade keep executing, so meta transactions already in flight across the upgrade boundary still complete. The `Action::DelegateV2` and `VersionedDelegateActionPayload` types stay in the codebase to hold a place for a future delegate action version. Clients that decode `ActionsValidationError` should expect the new variant.
* Early chunk producer reassignment. A chunk producer that stops producing used to keep its chunk slots until the end of the epoch, because the kickout set only applies at an epoch boundary. The protocol now tracks per-shard production stats within the epoch and stops assigning new chunks to a producer on a shard once it has missed at least 100 chunks there and its produced-to-expected ratio on that shard has fallen below 80%. The freed slot goes to a healthy producer. Stats never cross an epoch boundary, and a 1000-block grace window at the start of each epoch delays the first possible exclusion to roughly block 1000 of the epoch. A safety valve keeps the least-bad producer eligible when the rule would exclude every distinct producer on a shard, so a shard can never run out of chunk producers. The resulting assignment is precomputed per block and persisted in the `ChunkProducers` database column, keyed by the chunk's grandparent block, and chunk validation reads that row verbatim instead of re-sampling. Partial state witness, contract-accesses and contract-deploys network messages switch to their V2 wire variants at the same protocol version, since they now carry the grandparent anchor needed to resolve the producer. See [Early chunk producer reassignment](https://github.com/near/nearcore/blob/master/docs/ChainSpec/EpochAndStaking/EpochManager.md#early-chunk-producer-reassignment).
* Rejected a `WithdrawFromGasKey` action nested inside a delegate action, with the new `ActionsValidationError::WithdrawFromGasKeyNotAllowedInDelegate` error. `WithdrawFromGasKey` stays valid as a top-level action; only the nesting is refused. The SPICE pending transaction queue scans only a transaction's top-level actions for `WithdrawFromGasKey`, so a nested one drains a gas key that the queue still counts as funded. Receipts created before the upgrade keep executing, so delegate actions already in flight across the upgrade boundary still complete. Clients that decode `ActionsValidationError` should expect the new variant.
* A `FunctionCall` to a contract whose compiled module fails to load now charges the contract-loading fee and aborts, instead of finalizing as a zero-gas no-op. The fee is `contract_loading_base` plus `contract_loading_bytes` per byte of contract code, and it is burned even though the call runs no contract code. The call failed before this change too, so the only difference is that the caller now pays for the loading work. ([#15923](https://github.com/near/nearcore/pull/15923), [#16315](https://github.com/near/nearcore/pull/16315))
* Fixed a `FunctionCall` to a just-distributed global contract failing when the call runs in the same chunk as the distribution receipt and the compiled contract is not in the node's contract cache. The distribution now records the code with the chunk's contract tracker, as a regular `DeployContract` already does, so the call finds the code instead of failing with `CodeDoesNotExist`. ([#16371](https://github.com/near/nearcore/pull/16371))
* Fixed two ML-DSA-65 cost-charging issues, both of which are no-ops for the classical signature schemes where the relevant quantities coincide. Gas keys now price the exec (storage) fee on the on-trie identifier length (32-byte key hash for ML-DSA-65) and the send (transmission) fee on the wire length, instead of pricing the exec fee on the wire length. Meta transactions now meter the inner `DelegateAction` signature verification compute on the receiver shard that actually runs the verification, instead of the signer shard, so it counts against the right shard's compute limit. ([#16064](https://github.com/near/nearcore/pull/16064))
* Added the `sha3_256`, `sha3_384` and `sha3_512` host functions so contracts can compute FIPS-202 SHA-3 digests. Each takes the input either from memory or from a register and writes the digest (32, 48 or 64 bytes respectively) into a register. `sha3_256` costs a base of ~5.88 Ggas plus ~21.5 Mgas per input byte; `sha3_384` and `sha3_512` cost a base of ~5.81 Ggas plus ~36.6 Mgas per input byte. ([#16006](https://github.com/near/nearcore/pull/16006), [#16029](https://github.com/near/nearcore/pull/16029))
* Limited the total number of WASM locals in a contract to at most one local per two bytes of contract code. This size-dependent limit applies alongside the existing absolute limit of 1,000,000 locals per contract. [#16348](https://github.com/near/nearcore/pull/16348)
* Stabilized universal accounts: a `0u` account scheme that unifies implicit and contract-created (deterministic) account creation under one post-quantum-safe derivation. See [#16096](https://github.com/near/nearcore/issues/16096) for the full set of changes.
* A `FunctionCall` action with an empty `method_name` is now rejected at action validation with the new `ActionsValidationError::FunctionCallEmptyMethodName` error, so the transaction is refused before it is admitted. Previously such a transaction was admitted and failed on-chain in the VM with `MethodResolveError::MethodEmptyName`, still burning gas. Clients that decode `ActionsValidationError` should expect the new variant. ([#16089](https://github.com/near/nearcore/pull/16089))
* Capped the total number of storage entries carried by the state-init actions in one receipt at 1_500, counted across the receipt and into nested delegate actions. A receipt over the limit is rejected at action validation with the new `ActionsValidationError::TotalNumberOfStateInitEntriesExceeded` error. ([#16408](https://github.com/near/nearcore/pull/16408))

# Non-protocol Changes
* The `ChunkProducers` database column is now created by every build rather than only by nightly builds, which raises `DB_VERSION` from 49 to 50. A node started read-write migrates its hot and cold databases in place on startup; the migration only creates the column family and rewrites no data. A read-only process cannot create a column family, so a node opened read-only against a version-49 database will refuse to start. Start the node read-write once before pointing a read-only process at the data directory. ([#16301](https://github.com/near/nearcore/pull/16301))
* State sync now verifies reconstructed shard data against the next new chunk before block sync. A mismatch stops the node and preserves the data directory for diagnosis instead of attributing the failure to the chunk producer. ([#15994](https://github.com/near/nearcore/issues/15994))
* Removed the option to disable state snapshots. Nodes now always take a state snapshot every epoch, which is what lets them serve state parts to peers over decentralized state sync and is required by cloud archival. **Config change:** the `store.state_snapshot_config` field is gone, along with its `state_snapshot_type` values `Enabled`/`Disabled` and the legacy aliases `EveryEpoch`/`ForReshardingOnly`. A `config.json` that still contains `store.state_snapshot_config` keeps loading (the field is ignored), but a node that previously set it to `Disabled` (or `ForReshardingOnly`) will now take snapshots every epoch. Offline tools such as `fork-network` continue to run without snapshots.
* Removed the long-deprecated `num_block_producer_seats_per_shard`, `avg_hidden_validator_seats_per_shard`, and `num_chunk_only_producer_seats` fields from `EpochConfig`. They were given serde defaults in 2.12 and are unused. Existing epoch-config JSON files that still contain these keys keep loading, as the keys are now ignored. ([#15481](https://github.com/near/nearcore/issues/15481))
* Removed centralized (external-storage) state sync. Nodes now always sync state from peers, which has been the default for a long time. **Breaking config change:** `state_sync.sync` no longer accepts `ExternalStorage`; a node whose `config.json` still sets `"state_sync": {"sync": {"ExternalStorage": ... }}` will fail to start. Remove the `state_sync.sync` block (peer-based sync is the default) before upgrading. The deprecated `--state-sync-bucket` flag and the `state-parts-dump-check` tool are also removed. Dumping state to external storage (`state_sync.dump`) is unchanged.
* Added optional pagination to `EXPERIMENTAL_view_access_key_list` and the `view_access_key_list` query. The request takes `after_key` and `limit`, and the response returns `last_key` to fetch the following page. A new node-config knob `view_access_keys_limit` (default 100) bounds the number of keys returned per response; when unset (`null`) it falls back to the default of 100. **Behavioral change:** an *unpaginated* `view_access_key_list` request (no `limit`/`after_key`) now fails for any account holding more than `view_access_keys_limit` (default 100) access keys; such callers must switch to paginated requests. A paginated request whose `limit` exceeds the configured bound is clamped down to it rather than rejected. Operators can raise or lower the bound via `view_access_keys_limit`.
* Transaction-status timeouts (`tx`, `EXPERIMENTAL_tx_status`, and `send_tx`/`broadcast_tx_commit` with `wait_until`) now carry a `cause` in the `TIMEOUT_ERROR`'s `info` payload explaining how far the transaction got: `NOT_OBSERVED`, `PENDING` (with the last-known status), `DOES_NOT_TRACK_SHARD`, or `ERROR` (with `debug_info`). The `info` payload is absent on responses from older nodes, so clients should treat it as optional. Previously the timeout gave no detail.
* Added three Prometheus metrics for the blocks delay tracker: `near_blocks_delay_tracker_entries` (gauge, labelled by map), `near_blocks_delay_tracker_refused_blocks_total` (labelled by reason), and `near_blocks_delay_tracker_missing_entries_total` (labelled by mark). The tracker now records a block only while its height is within `[head - 50, head + 500)` and only up to 8 blocks per height, so `/debug/api/chain_processing_status` no longer lists blocks far from the head. Its `blocks_delay_tracker` error logs about a block that "was not marked received" are now a counter and a debug log, since a missing entry is expected once tracking is bounded.
* Raised the minimum supported Rust version to 1.95.0. Building `nearcore` from source now requires a Rust 1.95.0 toolchain.
* `tools/debug-ui` now builds with Vite instead of the unmaintained Create React App (`react-scripts`). Build output layout and the port 3000 dev server are unchanged, so deployment needs no change. Building now requires Node `^20.19.0 || >=22.12.0`. ([#16175](https://github.com/near/nearcore/pull/16175))
* Stabilized `EXPERIMENTAL_tx_status` and renamed it to `tx_status`. `EXPERIMENTAL_tx_status` keeps working as a deprecated alias, with the same request and response types. **Metrics change:** the `near_rpc_wait_until_count` metric now labels `tx`, `tx_status` and `EXPERIMENTAL_tx_status` separately; previously both `tx` and `EXPERIMENTAL_tx_status` were counted under the `tx_status` label. ([#16270](https://github.com/near/nearcore/pull/16270))
* `DBCol::EpochLightClientBlocks` now holds a versioned `StoredLightClientBlock` instead of the `LightClientBlockView` RPC type, which raises `DB_VERSION` from 50 to 51. A node started read-write migrates its hot database in place on startup, rewriting one row per epoch; the column holds a few thousand rows in total. The column is never garbage collected, so its rows were written by binaries going back to 2020 and appear in several borsh layouts; the migration reads each of them and rewrites it as the versioned type. A row that no layout reads stops the migration and names its epoch id rather than being guessed at. ([#16394](https://github.com/near/nearcore/pull/16394))

# Protocol upgrade voting

This release upgrades the protocol version from 86 to 88 in two steps.
Voting for protocol version 87 will start on Wednesday November 4th 00:00 UTC.
Voting for protocol version 88 will start on Friday November 6th 00:00 UTC.
To continue participating in consensus, you need to upgrade your node before voting for protocol version 87 starts.

If voting succeeds in one epoch, each protocol upgrade is expected to happen 7-14 hours after the voting epoch ends.

# Release notes

A patch release on top of 2.2.1 with the October 2026 out-of-band .NET security updates. See the [Microsoft announcement](https://devblogs.microsoft.com/dotnet/dotnet-october-2026-oob-security-updates/) for details of the fixed vulnerabilities.

There are no Nethermind code, database-format, or configuration changes, so you can upgrade in place from any 2.2.x version. Consensus behavior and fork schedules are the same as in 2.2.1.

## Overview

2 changes since 2.2.1:

- **.NET 10.0.14 runtime in Docker images and binaries**: Docker images are now based on `mcr.microsoft.com/dotnet/aspnet:10.0.14-resolute` (`-resolute-chiseled` for the chiseled variant). The self-contained binaries are built with SDK 10.0.403 and bundle the 10.0.14 runtime. Docker users only need to pull the new tag (#15251)
- **.NET packages updated to 10.0.14**: ASP.NET Core DataProtection, Microsoft.Extensions.\*, System.Security.Cryptography.\*, System.IO.Hashing, System.CommandLine and others (#15211)

## Build signatures

The packages are signed with the following OpenPGP key: `AD12 7976 5093 C675 9CD8 A400 24A7 7461 6F1E 617E`

## What's Changed

- chore(deps): update .NET packages by @rubo in https://github.com/NethermindEth/nethermind/pull/15211
- chore: update Dockerfiles to .NET 10.0.14 by @stdevMac in https://github.com/NethermindEth/nethermind/pull/15251

**Full Changelog**: https://github.com/NethermindEth/nethermind/compare/2.2.1...2.2.2
